audits.title: 929 An Audit of the Perioperative Clinical Assessment and Documentation of Delirium in Older Patients Following Vascular Surgery
audits.standard: Centre for Perioperative Care: daily delirium screening with a validated tool such as the 4-AT in patients 65 and over
audits.setting: Vascular surgery, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, patients aged 65 and over

cycle1.result: 4-AT screening in only 39.2% (n=20), on average 90 hours post-operatively; never documented in consultant-led post-operative review (100%, n=51).

audits.intervention: Recommended: stakeholder discussion, the mantra 'Post-op bloods and 4AT', and education on the 4-AT proforma.
audits.other_findings: Delirium concerns documented 7 times, with 4-AT documented in 5 of these.
audits.citation: Chand C, McCarthy T, Anthony R. 929 An Audit of the Perioperative Clinical Assessment and Documentation of Delirium in Older Patients Following Vascular Surgery. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.278.

audits.title: Identification of Cognitive Vulnerability in Older Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Audit of Admission Screening
audits.standard: Trust standard: all patients aged ≥60 have a cognitive screen completed on presentation to the surgical assessment unit
audits.setting: Surgical assessment unit, acute general surgical pathway (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals)

cycle1.result: Cognitive screen documented in 38 (45%); not documented in 37 (44%); clerking documentation missing in 9 (11%).

audits.other_findings: Of those screened, 19 (50%) had an operation within seven days, compared with 8/37 (22%) without a screen. Further work on barriers and targeted education was recommended.
audits.citation: O’Hare H, Elliott R, Shah N. Identification of Cognitive Vulnerability in Older Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Audit of Admission Screening. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S327-S327. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11804.

audits.title: Cognitive assessment of elderly inpatients: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Guidance that cognitive assessment should be performed on admission
audits.setting: Elderly care ward, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Cognitive assessment documented on admission in 22%, rising to 56% by discharge.

audits.other_findings: Only patients over 75 were assessed; 75% of those had some impairment and 36.8% a new or suspected dementia diagnosis.
audits.citation: Shermon E, Vernon LO, McGrath AJ. Cognitive assessment of elderly inpatients: a clinical audit. Dement Geriatr Cogn Dis Extra. 2015;5(1):25-31. doi:10.1159/000369881. PMID: 25759716.

audits.title: Improving inpatient care for older adults: Implementing Dementia Commissioning for Quality and Innovation (CQUIN).
audits.standard: Dementia CQUIN targets for dementia assessment completion

cycle1.result: Completion rate for dementia CQUIN assessments 27%.

audits.intervention: Changes to working practices suggested by junior doctors and nurses, informed by interviews; involvement of the multidisciplinary team.
audits.other_findings: Involving the multidisciplinary team produced the most significant improvement.
audits.citation: Harrison JR. Improving inpatient care for older adults: Implementing Dementia Commissioning for Quality and Innovation (CQUIN). BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2017;6(1):u212202.w4875. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u212202.w4875. PMID: 28607682.

audits.title: Documentation of cognitive impairment screening amongst older hospitalised Australians: a prospective clinical record audit.
audits.standard: Documentation of cognitive impairment screening in hospital inpatients aged 65 years and over
audits.setting: One Australian public hospital, inpatients aged 65 and over

cycle1.result: Screening for cognitive impairment documented in 34.5% (n = 57).

audits.other_findings: 72% (n = 78) of unscreened patients were cognitively impaired on MoCA; staff cited lack of time and poor knowledge as barriers.
audits.citation: Rice R, Bryant J, Fisher RS. Documentation of cognitive impairment screening amongst older hospitalised Australians: a prospective clinical record audit. BMC Geriatr. 2023;23(1):672. doi:10.1186/s12877-023-04394-z. PMID: 37853320.

audits.title: Improving Mental Status Questionnaire (MSQ) completion on admission to the Acute Surgical Receiving Unit (ASRU), Ninewells Hospital, Dundee.
audits.standard: Mental Status Questionnaire completed on admission for 95% of patients aged 75 or over (project target)
audits.setting: Acute Surgical Receiving Unit, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee, tertiary centre

cycle1.result: MSQ completion 14.99% (16.6% and 13.3% in the two five-day periods); no patient had a formal delirium diagnosis despite a mean of 5.4 of 12 risk factors

audits.intervention: Sticker listing all 10 MSQ questions in the admission document, with signage, email to junior doctors and advanced nurse practitioners briefing new staff

cycle2.result: Average MSQ completion 81.33%; 100% on two days; 40% on the first day

audits.other_findings: Compliance dipped at the weekend and with junior doctor rotation; there was no clear pathway for patients with low MSQ scores.
audits.citation: Okwemba S, Copeland L. Improving Mental Status Questionnaire (MSQ) completion on admission to the Acute Surgical Receiving Unit (ASRU), Ninewells Hospital, Dundee. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u205217.w2159. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u205217.w2159. PMID: 27493742.
